A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoDi research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably despite additions and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original ConsiStory+ benchmark results, component and parameter ablations, runtime measurements and qualitative generation results, including appendix examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a human-preference study, an OT-versus-cosine comparison and further qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: The core IT/IR algorithm and equations remain unchanged. Section 4.4 adds an extension that applies IT and IR independently to each subject; Figure 12 describes a clothing-preservation variant that expands the foreground mask. These are limited adaptations of the existing procedure.

E1.justification: The ConsiStory+ benchmark and existing long-story examples are retained. Sections 4.4–4.5 add limited qualitative scenarios requiring simultaneous consistency of multiple subjects and preservation of one identity across changing styles, extending the previously demonstrated task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds qualitative comparisons with UNO and UNO(face) in Figure 10 and a cosine-matching alternative in Appendix F. Vanilla SDXL is removed from the confidence-threshold comparison, matching v1 Figure 6 to v2 Figure 8. The main Table 1 comparator set is unchanged; 1Prompt1Story is a renamed presentation of the existing baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.6 and Appendix H introduce a distinct human-evaluation protocol: 39 participants choose among four methods using 30 randomly sampled prompt sets, each containing four prompts. v2 also introduces Flux-based testing and a clothing-mask adjustment. The original automated benchmark settings remain, while Figure 1's separate pose-fidelity evaluation is omitted.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens supplementary investigation through a direct OT-versus-cosine ablation, a Flux architecture-generalization demonstration, and multi-subject, cross-style and clothing-consistency case studies. Existing IT/IR, transition-point and alpha ablations remain. The confidence-threshold analysis is retained but loses its Vanilla SDXL comparison.

E5.justification: Both versions specify identical noise seeds across methods without reporting repeated-run counts or variability estimates. v2's preference percentages and additional comparisons introduce no confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the relocated runtime results retain their numerical values. New results include CoDi's 45.21% human preference versus StoryDiffusion's 21.20% (v2 Table 3), OT versus cosine pose diversity of 0.0758 versus 0.0704 (Appendix F), and additional qualitative comparisons and applications. v1 Figure 1's pose-fidelity/diversity values and the threshold-sweep results for Vanilla SDXL are removed.

T1.justification: Equations 1–21 retain the same OT formulation, attention operations, saliency calculation and pose-metric derivation. No new formal assumptions, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claim that training-free, two-stage CoDi balances subject consistency and pose diversity. The introduction removes the specific claim of best performance on pose fidelity and pose diversity, replacing it with a claim about the consistency–diversity trade-off.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking independent subject processing to reduced interference, IR to style variation, and OT to better structural alignment than cosine matching. Applicability discussions extend to Flux and training-based competitors. The existing mask-quality limitation is unchanged, while Appendix F introduces internally contradictory wording about pose preservation.

D1.justification: Figure 12 adds instructions to include clothing descriptions and adjust the subject-mask threshold. Appendix H and Figure 14 document the user-study sampling, evaluation criteria and example questionnaire. Existing implementation formulas, default settings, hardware measurements and code link are retained; detailed Flux adaptation settings are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including UNO, Detail++ and additional diffusion/control-related works. Appendix E extends positioning to a training-based competitor, but the training-based/training-free taxonomy and the main novelty argument remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative are retained, with local wording and terminology edits, a CoDi title prefix and conference information. The runtime discussion moves to Appendix D, new experimental subsections and appendices are inserted, and acknowledgments and an LLM-writing disclosure are added.

P2.justification: The visual presentation expands substantially with new application and comparison grids, a questionnaire figure and a preference table. Figure 1 replaces its numerical pose panel with a scatterplot redisplaying benchmark results. The threshold plot changes its axis range and legend while omitting SDXL, and conference formatting reflows and relocates retained figures and tables.

improvement.justification: The new human-preference study, OT-versus-cosine ablation and broader qualitative demonstrations strengthen support beyond v1's retained benchmark evidence. The gains are limited by sparse implementation and uncertainty reporting for the additions. Removing the SDXL threshold comparison and introducing contradictory explanatory prose in Appendix F offset some benefit, supporting a modest net improvement.
